diagnostic_bottleneck: None; visual phenotype of 'green ear' is pathognomonic for Downy Mildew in Pearl Millet.

final_decision.reason: The observed transformation of the panicle into a leafy, vegetative structure (green ear) is the specific identity gate for Downy Mildew. This morphology explicitly contradicts the anti-features for Blast, Smut, and Leaf Spots, and lacks the sclerotium or honeydew characteristics of Ergot.

symptom_class.description: Transformation of the panicle into a leafy, vegetative structure (green ear).

geometry.description: The affected panicle has lost its compact cylindrical form and expanded into a disorganized mass of narrow, leaf-like structures.

surface.description: The surface of the abnormal structure consists of numerous small, green, leaf-like appendages rather than grain-bearing florets.

distribution.description: The abnormality is confined to the terminal panicle of the affected plant.

reproductive_structure.description: The panicle is transformed into a leafy/vegetative structure. Normal grains are absent from the affected head.

present: Absence of normal grains on affected panicle
absent: Normal grain development on affected panicle
not_visible: Downy/velvety growth (underside of leaves or inside the green ear)
